label: Colour contrast and link distinction
description: Darker light-theme link blue, a text-only accent colour that stays readable on the dark background, no opacity on the footer licence text, and underlined in-text links.
problem: In the light theme links (#3479c4 on white) and the footer licence text are just under 4.5:1. In the dark theme the purple accent (#ac1d94 on #222) is about 2.5:1 for the active nav item, the date and the logo suffix, and in-text links are told apart from surrounding text by colour alone.
steps: Open the home page in both frames (use the Home page in the Page menu).
Light theme: look at the footer licence text and the "CC BY 4.0" link. Before is pale grey with a lighter blue link; after is darker.
Press the Dark theme button. Look at the date line under the logo, the "FOSDEM'27" suffix and the current item in the top navigation. Before is a dim purple; after is a lighter pink.
Open News or FAQ. In-text links are underlined after the change, plain coloured text before.
Optional, to measure it: run axe DevTools (or the browser's built-in contrast checker) on the same page in each frame, or open a side in its own window first.
expectedBefore: axe reports colour-contrast on every page in both themes and link-in-text-block in the dark theme.
expectedAfter: axe reports neither rule on any of the 7 pages checked, in light or dark.

label: Visible keyboard focus
description: An explicit 3px focus ring in both themes (blue in light, yellow in dark) instead of the browser's default 1px ring.
problem: The site never sets a focus style, so keyboard users get the browser default: a 1px ring in a fixed blue (#005FCC). On the dark background that is about 2.6:1, under the 3:1 needed for a focus indicator.
steps: Open the FAQ page. Click once on empty page space inside the Before frame (not on a link) so it has focus.
Press Tab several times and watch the ring around each link and button. Note how thin and dim it is.
Do the same in the After frame. Click on empty space first, then Tab.
Press the Dark theme button and repeat in both frames. The Before ring nearly disappears on the dark background; the After ring is yellow.
The keyboard is not mirrored between frames, so test each one yourself, or use Open in a new window.
expectedBefore: A thin default ring that is under 3:1 against the dark background.
expectedAfter: A 3px ring on every focusable element, at least 3:1 in both themes.

label: SkipTo skip-link menu
description: Vendored paypal/skipto 4.1.7. The first Tab stop on every page is a menu of the page's landmarks and headings.
problem: The site has no skip link, so keyboard and screen reader users must tab through the whole header navigation on every page to reach the content.
steps: Open the FAQ page. Click on empty page space inside the Before frame, then press Tab once. Focus lands on the "FOSDEM'27" logo link; there is no way to jump past the navigation.
Click on empty space in the After frame, then press Tab once. A "Skip To Content" button appears at the top.
Press Enter to open the menu. It lists landmarks (main, navigation, contentinfo) and the page headings.
Choose "main" with the arrow keys and Enter. Focus moves to the main content. Press Escape to close the menu without choosing.
The keyboard is not mirrored between frames, so test each one yourself, or use Open in a new window.
expectedBefore: The first Tab stop is the logo link. No skip mechanism exists.
expectedAfter: The first Tab stop is a "Skip To Content" button; Enter opens a menu of at least 3 destinations; Escape closes it.

label: Link hover and visited colours
description: Visited and hover colours for text links (4.5:1 or better in both themes); hover also thickens the underline.
problem: Text links look the same whether or not you have visited them, and hovering the footer links changes nothing, so there is no feedback that a link is interactive or already read.
steps: Open the FAQ page and scroll to the footer. Hover the "CC BY 4.0" link in the Before frame: nothing changes.
Hover it in the After frame: the colour changes and the underline gets thicker.

Visited colours: click a text link in the After frame (for example one inside an FAQ answer), then come back. The link is now a different colour from an unvisited one. A browser only shows visited colours for pages in its own history, so this cannot be shown in a fresh profile or by screenshot.
Press the Dark theme button and repeat. Both states must stay readable.
expectedBefore: No hover change on footer links and no visited colour is defined.
expectedAfter: Hover changes colour and uses a 2px underline; the visited colour is at least 4.5:1, in light and dark. (The automated check reads the defined visited colour, because browsers hide :visited from scripts.)

label: Light choice overrides a dark OS (forge PR #11)
description: A one-line CSS change so the dark-mode media query respects an explicit Light choice. This is the pull request exactly as submitted, built from its own head commit against the code it was written for, so Before and After use the old layout and pages. Upstream main already contains the same fix, shown in the third column of the results.
problem: When the operating system is in dark mode and a visitor picks Light with the site's own toggle, the page stays dark: the prefers-color-scheme rule sets the dark colours on :root whatever the site's choice is.
steps: Set your operating system to dark mode (or press Simulate a dark-mode OS above) and reload.
Press the Light theme button above. Both frames reload with the site's choice set to Light.
Before: the page stays dark, or is partly dark, even though Light was chosen. After: it is fully light.
To see that current upstream main already behaves like After, open the Home page of any other change in this viewer, with the same settings.
expectedBefore: The page is dark although Light was chosen.

label: Everything together
description: Upstream with all of the changes above merged. A merge conflict here fails the build, so it also shows whether the changes still fit together.
problem: The changes are separate branches. This checks they work when applied together, not only one at a time.
steps: Open the Home page and work through the steps of each change above in the After frame.
Press Tab: the first stop should be the Skip To Content button, and it and every later stop should show the focus ring.
expectedBefore: Every problem described above is present.
expectedAfter: All four automated checks pass on the merged result.
